questions.question_text:
A solid has two identical parallel square bases joined by four rectangular side faces.
What is the solid?

options.why: Treats the square base shape as sufficient to identify a pyramid and ignores the two parallel bases.
Names triangular bases instead of the square bases given.
Changes the given square bases to a triangular base and assumes an apex that is not present.

questions.solution_text: It is a square-based prism because it has two identical parallel polygonal bases joined by rectangular sides.

options.text: It is a pyramid because its side faces meet at one apex.
It is a prism because it has flat faces.
options.why: Treats having flat faces as sufficient, although both families have flat faces.

options.text: It is a prism because its base is a pentagon.
options.why: Uses the base shape but ignores that there is only one base and an apex.

options.text: It is a pyramid because it has two matching bases.
options.why: Attributes the prism base property to a pyramid.

questions.solution_text: The side faces meet at a single apex, so the solid is a pyramid.

questions.question_text:
A solid has two identical parallel hexagonal ends joined by rectangular side faces.
What must be true?

options.why: Uses pyramid even though a pyramid has only one base.
This names triangular bases instead of the hexagonal ends stated in the question.
Ignores that two matching parallel bases determine a prism.

questions.solution_text: Two identical parallel hexagonal bases identify a hexagonal prism.

questions.question_text:
A solid has one triangular base and three triangular side faces meeting at one apex.
Does it have a uniform cross-section parallel to its base?

options.text: No, because the parallel cross-sections become smaller towards the apex.
Yes, because every parallel cross-section is triangular.
options.why: Checks only the shape and ignores that uniform cross-sections must also have the same size.

options.text: Yes, because all its faces are triangles.
options.why: Confuses the shapes of the faces with whether parallel cross-sections are identical.

options.text: No, because the parallel cross-sections become larger towards the apex.
options.why: Reverses the direction in which a pyramid tapers.

questions.solution_text: No. It is a triangular pyramid, and its parallel cross-sections become smaller towards the apex.

questions.question_text:
A solid has two identical parallel nonagonal ends joined by nine rectangular side faces. It rests on a rectangular side face.
Which classification is correct?

options.why: Ignores the two parallel bases and incorrectly assumes the side faces meet at an apex.
Names the solid after the side face it rests on instead of its identical opposite end faces.
Treats the resting face as the base and assumes an apex despite the two matching nonagonal ends.

questions.solution_text: It is a nonagonal prism because its two identical parallel polygonal bases are nonagons joined by rectangular sides.

questions.question_text:
A solid has one octagonal base and eight triangular side faces meeting at one apex. It rests on a triangular side face.
Which classification is correct?

options.why: Uses the base shape but ignores the single base and the triangular side faces meeting at an apex.
Names the solid after a triangular side face instead of its octagonal base.
Mistakes a triangular side face for one of two matching triangular bases and ignores the apex.

questions.solution_text: It is an octagonal pyramid because its triangular side faces meet at one apex above a single octagonal base.
